statement_en: In the product measure space $$(\mathbb{R}^2,\mathcal{L}\otimes \mathcal{L},m^2),$$ where $(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{L},m)$ is the Lebesgue measure space, the set $[0,1]\times\{0\}$ has $m^2$-measure zero because $$m^2([0,1]\times\{0\})=m([0,1])m(\{0\})=0.$$ However, since there exists a nonmeasurable subset of $[0,1]$, such as a Vitali set $V\subset [0,1]$, one can form $V\times \{0\}\subset [0,1]\times\{0\}$, and this set is not an element of $\mathcal{L}\otimes \mathcal{L}$.
